grh_b64531ffb459d695f980.title: Bensons Inventions
paragraphs: Buzz Benson is Rivers End's much-ridiculed school janitor and amateur inventor, better known for failed gadgets and pranks than for serious ability. Dr. Christian discovers that Buzz has a genuine interest in chemistry and quietly coaches him. When word spreads that Buzz has invented a revolutionary 'chemical motor' and that Christian plans to send him to New York, townsmen who had mocked Buzz suddenly call him a genius, argue that his discovery belongs in Rivers End and begin maneuvering for a share of the supposed fortune. Their enthusiasm grows into a public meeting built around developing the motor locally. Christian finally exposes the mistake: he never vouched for Buzz's chemical motor at all. The real achievement is a useful precipitation process Buzz discovered accidentally, and Christian has arranged for a pharmaceutical company in New York to give the young man a job where he can learn the business. By letting the rumor run, Christian reveals how quickly the town's contempt turned to self-interested praise once money seemed involved and makes the would-be backers confront how little they actually knew about the boy they had dismissed.

grh_b6d42831b322324b1c60.title: Lucky Jordan
paragraphs: Self-centered racketeer Lucky Jordan is drafted into the Army and immediately looks for a way around service, only to become entangled with a stolen briefcase containing sensitive military plans. At first Lucky treats the papers like any other commodity and considers selling them for a fortune, while Jill tries to make him understand that the war and the country's survival affect even a man who believes only in himself. Rival gangsters and enemy agents pursue the plans, forcing Lucky to use the same street instincts that built his criminal career to recover and protect them. By the end, his cynicism has given way to a reluctant sense of responsibility, and he chooses his country over the payoff he once wanted.

grh_b6eb15bc3cb387fa0f03.title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes-The Second Generation
paragraphs: In retirement, Holmes is approached by Miss Norton, Irene Adler's daughter, who persuades him and Watson to recover a filigree box from the home of a wealthy collector by claiming it contains compromising letters. During the burglary the collector's butler tries to exploit the situation, steal valuable jewels and kill Holmes and Watson while blaming the intruders. Holmes survives, discovers that Miss Norton used him as a cat's-paw and that the box concealed the stolen Kippenja emerald, and returns the gem. grh_b6d0ac8f21d918284fae.title: Murder in the Casbah
paragraphs: Holmes travels to Algiers to find Douglas Milton, the long-missing heir to the Montrevor estate, and locates a man in the Casbah who claims the name. After violence surrounding his companion Aisha, Holmes gets the supposed heir to the British consulate and deliberately has him swear a legal statement to his identity. Holmes then reveals that he is an impostor and deserter: the real Milton was a painter with a trained eye for color, while this man cannot distinguish red from green. The Foreign Legion closes in as the false Milton tries to escape, ending a scheme built on impersonation, forgery and perjury.

grh_b626dcf947e0e84e8c69.title: Myra Barker
paragraphs: Britt meets the independent Myra Barker after she borrows Scar, and the two agree to keep each other company so friends will stop trying to marry them off. Their practical arrangement turns into genuine love and Britt proposes, but Myra doubts either of them is ready to give up a wandering life. She tests him with a false story that a sheriff needs his help, and Britt realizes that even if he married her he would still be pulled toward the next call for adventure. Remembering how his restless father left his mother lonely, he rides away rather than risk doing the same to Myra.

grh_b6ecc34b9e56457e6a1a.title: Robert Lane Intern Shirks Duties
paragraphs: Intern Robert Lane abandons a special hospital assignment and nearly costs a cardiac patient his life, yet refuses to explain where he has been, so Kildare covers for him while trying to discover the cause. A $5,000 life-insurance policy, a notebook of patients and a missing analytical spectroscope lead Kildare to the truth: Lane has been practicing medicine illegally on the side and pawned the hospital instrument for $300 because he is supporting his pregnant sister Margaret after her husband deserted her. Kildare brings him back to Blair as Margaret goes into labor, while Gillespie quietly retrieves the spectroscope and converts the $300 into a loan payable after Lane graduates. With the financial pressure exposed and his sister safely delivered of a son, Lane is able to return to his internship and continue toward becoming a doctor.

grh_b64ba543792583e27780.title: The Failure
paragraphs: Jeff Fowler has recovered from a long illness but is unable to return to his former work, leaving him desperate to prove he can support his wife Alice and their children through writing. He pours himself into poetry and serious manuscripts, suffers rejection after rejection and comes to see himself as a miserable failure. During a visit, Dr. Christian hears Jeff improvise a fantasy adventure for the children and notices how completely the story captures them. He recognizes that Jeff's natural gift is not the literary form he has been forcing, but the children's stories he tells with ease and imagination. With Jeff's permission Christian acts as his representative and has those stories prepared for publication. He then reminds Jeff that Hans Christian Andersen also pursued other literary ambitions before his fairy tales became his lasting achievement. A publisher accepts Jeff's first collection of Winky and Blinky adventures, and Jeff finally understands that reaching the hearts of children is his real vocation rather than a failure.
GRH catalogs [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]]'s "The Failure" for November 8, 1944, as episode 311.
